notes:
The popup can stay open beside your work and a prompt can press Enter for you, so a run of quick replies to an agent is one click each. Builds on [v0.2.21](https://github.com/bekalpaslan/promptline/releases/tag/v0.2.21).

### Popup

- **Keep open.** Press **Ctrl+K**, or the toggle beside the search box, and the popup stays up beside your work: it no longer hides when you click away or after a paste, and it pastes into the last window you used. The hotkey brings it back to the front; **Esc** closes it and ends Keep open, and every summon starts without it.
- **To know the last window you used, Promptline now follows which window is in front while it runs.** It keeps only the latest one in memory, ignores its own windows and the taskbar, and stores and sends nothing.
- **Drag the hint bar to move the popup.** The whole bar at the bottom is a handle; while the popup is kept open, a hand in its corner marks it.
- **See the whole clipboard.** **Ctrl+↓**, or a click on the clipboard line, drops the clipboard down as it will paste: numbered lines, indentation kept, hidden control characters shown. It shows up to 400 lines, and the rest still paste. **Esc** or **Enter** puts it away.
- **Prompts set to Auto enter say so** before you press anything: a ↵ beside the title, and "paste and enter" in the hint bar.

### Manager

- **Auto enter.** A switch under a prompt's text makes the popup press Enter after pasting it, for quick replies like "LGTM" or `/clear`; it lights up in amber while on. A copy never presses Enter.
- **Auto enter is yours alone.** It is saved in your library (a new `autoEnter` field in `snippets.json`, left out while off) and never in a pack file or an export, so a pack someone shares can't arrive set to send a command.
- **Copy a prompt without opening it.** Every card in a pack's or group's overview has a copy button (or press **Ctrl+C** on a focused card), and the editor's Prompt panel has one too. They copy what the popup would paste, with your clipboard filled in; fill-in fields stay as typed for you to fill in.
- **One list shows every prompt.** With **Display → One list**, the pane shows all your prompts as cards, each naming its pack and group, instead of the last pack you had open.
- **A renamed pack's file now follows its name.** A pack made as "New pack" and renamed gets a file named after it (`workflow-prompts.json` rather than `new-pack-3.json`). Only files the app named itself move; a file you or an agent named, or one outside the packs folder, stays where it is. Packs renamed before this update keep their old file names until you rename them again.
